title: ZKnowledgeCompounding 开源候选覆盖调研
summary: 调研 5 个开源项目（Semantica / TrustGraph / Utopia / OpenWiki / gbrain）对 ZKC 22 个技术调研 topic 的覆盖情况。结论：无整体替代方案；Utopia（双时态/本地优先/人审蒸馏）、OpenWiki（OKF/Grounded Claims）、gbrain（混合检索/信号探测）在若干子系统可直接借鉴；双轨静态/动态建模与稀缺注意力调度无人覆盖，需自建。

concepts.value: ZKC needs dual-track (static/dynamic) capture + compounding transform (distill/combine/connect/model) + scarce-resource scheduling; this report evaluates OSS coverage of the 22 derived topics.
Coverage scored native / adapted / absent / unknown per topic; an unobserved capability is reported as unknown, never as absent.
Whole-product adoption is rejected; unit-capability reuse is the preferred ownership posture.
problem-discovery / selection phase for the ZKC architecture; findings are point-in-time and pre-MVP.

cards.title: Semantica — graph-native KG infrastructure
cards.summary: Graph + triplet + vector stores, LLM ontology generation, PROV-O provenance. Strong on T1.1/T2.1/T2.2/T6.1; absent on T0.1 (dual-track) and T5.x (attention). Server/Docker oriented.

cards.title: TrustGraph — semantic agent governance platform
cards.summary: RDF 1.2 named graphs + OWL enforcement + PROV-O; Knowledge Lifecycle Management at collection level; self-host open-weight inference. Scheduling & local-first unverified.

cards.title: Utopia — enterprise world model / bitemporal KG
cards.summary: Bitemporal knowledge graph (fact validity + provenance), one Rust binary + one Postgres, air-gapped, human review queue for extraction merges. Strongest coverage of T1.2/T1.3/T3.1.

cards.title: OpenWiki — owned linked Markdown wiki (OKF implementation)
cards.summary: Distills multi-source raw into owned linked Markdown wiki; Grounded Claims bound to source (OKF v0.2); scheduled CI updates; 14 LLM providers. Concrete implementation of the PRD's OKF reference.

cards.title: gbrain — agent brain / hybrid retrieval
cards.summary: Hybrid retrieval (vector + keyword + graph, RRF), embedded PGLite/SQLite, signal-detector for attention-like signals, cron source pulls, LongMemEval eval. Closest to T5.1/T6.1.

claims.text: Semantica is graph-native infrastructure (graph + triplet + vector stores, Neo4j/Neptune, fastembed) with LLM-backed ontology generation and PROV-O provenance, but does not model node-level knowledge lifecycle/decay.

TrustGraph models knowledge as RDF 1.2 named graphs with OWL enforcement and PROV-O provenance, plus Knowledge Lifecycle Management at collection level; scheduling and local-first fitness are unverified (unknown).

Utopia implements a bitemporal knowledge graph (every fact carries validity window + provenance), ships as one Rust binary + one Postgres with air-gapped/offline capability, and includes a human review queue for extraction merges.

OpenWiki distills multi-source raw input into an owned linked Markdown wiki using Grounded Claims bound to source locations (OKF v0.2) with scheduled CI updates; it is a concrete implementation of the OKF format referenced in the PRD.

gbrain provides hybrid retrieval (vector + keyword + graph, RRF), embedded PGLite/SQLite storage, a signal-detector skill for attention-like signals, and cron-based source pulls with LongMemEval grounding eval.

None of the five candidates natively model ZKC's dual-track split between static (fact-type, long-lifecycle) and dynamic (survival-type, short-lifecycle) capture; all treat captured knowledge uniformly.
Only Utopia models node-level temporality (bitemporal validity); others model lifecycle only at collection/version level (TrustGraph) or not at all.
Explicit human review / grounding in distillation exists only in Utopia (review queue) and OpenWiki (Grounded Claims); the others automate extraction without a review loop.
Attention-signal modeling and recall/scheduling tuned to scarce attention are absent across all five; gbrain's signal-detector and cron pulls are the closest but are not compound-attention aware.
Local-first single-file deployment is achieved by none; Utopia (one binary + Postgres, air-gapped) and gbrain (embedded PGLite/SQLite) are the closest to self-host/offline.

Storage models diverge: Semantica and TrustGraph are native graph systems (Neo4j/Neptune; RDF named graphs); Utopia and gbrain use a relational core + vector (Postgres/pgvector, PGLite/SQLite); OpenWiki is document-based (Markdown + claim sidecars). No candidate is a single-file local-first store.

Lifecycle/decay is the weakest shared area. Only Utopia models node-level temporality (bitemporal validity + provenance + append-only decision ledger). TrustGraph offers collection-level lifecycle; OpenWiki offers claim-level stale_after; Semantica and gbrain do not model knowledge decay.

Distillation with a human-in-the-loop exists only in Utopia (review queue for reversible merges) and OpenWiki (Grounded Claims evidence reconciliation). Semantica/TrustGraph/gbrain automate extraction without an explicit review loop, so ZKC's required human-in-loop distillation is not covered off-the-shelf.

Local-first / offline capability: Utopia runs air-gapped as one binary + one Postgres; gbrain embeds PGLite/SQLite locally; Semantica/TrustGraph target Docker/K8s server deployment; OpenWiki is a local CLI writing to ~/.openwiki. None is a zero-dependency single-file store.

recommendations.text: No candidate is a drop-in replacement for ZKC. Recommend a unit-capability reuse strategy, not whole-product adoption: borrow Utopia's bitemporal storage + human-in-loop distillation as the lifecycle backbone, OpenWiki's Grounded-Claims/OKF pattern for the meta-cognition claim layer, and gbrain's hybrid retrieval + signal-detector for the scheduling/attention seam. The dual-track static/dynamic capture model and the scarce-attention scheduler must be built in-house — they are ZKC's core differentiator and are unaddressed by all five.

Before committing architecture, run a hands-on spike on the two most-aligned candidates (Utopia for bitemporal + human-in-loop; OpenWiki for OKF/Grounded Claims) to validate personal-use fitness, and resolve the two unknown TrustGraph criteria by direct inspection. Keep the ZKC dual-track and attention layers decoupled so they can sit on top of any chosen storage.

riskRegister.risk: Candidate capabilities may be over-fitted to enterprise/governance use cases, not personal knowledge compounding.
riskRegister.trigger: Selecting a candidate as the ZKC backbone without validating personal-use fitness.
riskRegister.impact: MVP solves the wrong problem; attention and lifecycle needs stay unmet.
riskRegister.mitigation: Run a personal-use spike on Utopia + OpenWiki before committing; keep the ZKC dual-track layer decoupled from any chosen storage.
riskRegister.residualRisk: Residual mismatch if the spike is skipped or scoped too narrowly.

riskRegister.risk: The sealed ledger captured anonymous GitHub stars; topicMatch is a heuristic and may misrank fit.
riskRegister.trigger: Treating stars / topicMatch as capability scores in the adoption decision.
riskRegister.impact: Mis-prioritized adoption and wasted integration effort.
riskRegister.mitigation: Use stars / topicMatch only as discovery signals; rely on evidence-backed claims and a hands-on spike for ranking.
riskRegister.residualRisk: Minor mis-prioritization remains if signals are overweighted.

riskRegister.risk: Two unknown criteria (TrustGraph scheduling, TrustGraph local-first) leave a coverage gap.
riskRegister.trigger: Reporting TrustGraph coverage without resolving the unknowns.
riskRegister.impact: Incomplete comparison for TrustGraph before any adoption decision.
riskRegister.mitigation: Flag as has-gaps; resolve via direct repo inspection or docs before final adoption.

riskRegister.risk: Compiler/ledger pins specific repo revisions; fast-moving repos may diverge from findings.
riskRegister.trigger: Basing architecture on the pinned 2026-10-28 snapshot without refresh.
riskRegister.impact: Findings age; APIs and capabilities change underfoot.
riskRegister.mitigation: Re-run collect before implementation; treat findings as point-in-time evidence.
riskRegister.residualRisk: Stale evidence if the ledger is not refreshed near build time.

informationGaps.rationale: Has information gaps: the sealed ledger left trustgraph scheduling and trustgraph local_first as unknown criteria; these must be resolved by direct inspection before any adoption decision.
